title: Healing Through Sound: Music Therapy
shared_passage: Listen to an interview with a music therapist. For questions 1 to 7, choose the correct answer (A, B, or C).

questions.question: What does Sarah say to describe music therapy?
options: It relies on listening to your favourite music.
It is designed to improve mental and physical health.
It's entertainment used for healing.

questions.question: What best distinguishes music therapy from casual listening?
options: Casual listening does not affect people's emotions.
Music therapy requires guidance.
Both are equally effective for therapy.

questions.question: According to Sarah, who can music therapy support?
options: Only people with emotional issues or brain injuries.
People suffering from anxiety and insomnia.
People with mental health or mobility issues.

questions.question: What progress did Mia make thanks to music therapy?
options: She improved her mobility and speech.
Singing helped her walk correctly again.
She fully recovered her speech.

questions.question: What emotional effects can music therapy have on patients?
options: It helps people be more focused.
Angry people can listen to an old favourite song and calm down.
Playing an instrument can help with anger or frustration.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT mentioned by Sarah as a common misconception?
options: Any type of music can help a patient.
It only works with people who believe in it.
You don't need to be musical to have therapy.

questions.question: What does Sarah say about the future of music therapy?
options: It is already becoming part of many care institutions.
There is still not enough scientific support.
It will replace traditional treatments for some conditions.
